title.narrative: Improving Water Supply and Hygiene Interventions for IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Buur Hakaba District

description.narrative:
ltpgtIn Somalia, a prolonged drought has resulted in water sources drying up, rising water prices, and extensive loss of livestock, hampering food production and placing immense pressure on already vulnerable communities’ ability to access food and water. By July 2022, an estimated 7.1 million people were in need of food assistance across the country, with over 2.1 million people classified in Integrated Food Security Classification (IPC) Phase 4 (Emergency) and more than 200,000 people likely experiencing Phase 5 (Catastrophic) levels of food insecurity. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibrimso-bidi-theme-font:minor-latin"gtConditions are particularly concerning in Buur Hakaba districts where malnutrition and mortality rates have surpassed emergency thresholds, alongside disease outbreaks, including cholera and measles. Findings from multiple sources indicate critical WASH situations across both district, particularly in internally displaced person (IDP) sites, hosting displaced populations from largely inaccessible areas, whose vulnerability was exacerbated due to extended periods of limited access to water and food insecurity in their places of origin and during displacement. Heightened physical vulnerabilities among drought-affected populations are likely driving the ongoing cholera and measles outbreaks and high incidence of diarrhea in the district, and when coupled with poor health services environment, are likely contributing to the severe nutrition, morbidity and mortality outcomes. Since access to safe and clean water is the main challenge faced by IDPs and the vulnerable poor host communities, provision of safe water is a key priority according to the local administration and well as the local community. Therefore, it is crucial to scale up water and sanitation interventions alongside other humanitarian assistance, without which a significant reduction in morbidity and mortality is highly unlikely. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibrimso-bidi-theme-font:minor-latin"gtIn Buur Hakaba district, displaced agropastoral households are camping in 2 IDP sites, namely Misaare and Aye Dhurey and 6 villages which include Ugari, 4 Goley, Baale, Banzole, Shidlow Nasiye and Gododey with extremely limited access to adequate safe water, sanitation and health services. The sites are verified by ltspan style="background:white"gtCommunity Empowerment and Social Development Organization lt/spangtand SOS in November 2022, hosting a total of 953 households (6,693 individuals) of which 55% are female and 45% male at the time (CCCM Cluster Somalia: IDP Sites in Buur Hakaba). These IDPs depend for their water needs on dilapidated, unprotected shallow wells and water pans. Both water sources are susceptible to contamination as all defecating and dumping sites are located in or along the waterways. As a result, outbreak of AWD and other waterborne diseases are common in the IDPs Sites. Considering pre-existing food insecurity and undernutrition has likely compromised their immunity, these IDPs are facing an elevated risk of mortality. Evidence to support this is: in Buur Hakaba a new ‘spike’ of cholera cases was recorded through April 2022 (WHO, Cholera - Somalia, Accessed on 15th August 2022). lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtThe objective of the project is to improve access to safe water, context specific appropriate sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion for conflict affected most vulnerable IDP households and host communities The objective will be achieved by (a) increasing access to adequate quantity of safe water for target IDPs, which is critical to help prevent the transmission and spread of diarrheal disease and support response to AWD outbreaks in IDP sites (b) Improving hygiene practices at camp level to curb the spread of waterborne diseases and (c) Improving awareness and knowledge through community health promotion.ltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gt
ltbrgtlt/pgt
